summary: WebSocket real-time updates feature validated end-to-end. Backend /api/ws endpoint accepts anonymous and JWT-authenticated connections, subscribe/unsubscribe/ping/get_status protocol works, and REST mutations (overtime create) trigger broadcasts that are delivered to subscribed WebSocket clients. Frontend Dashboard connects via WebSocketProvider, authenticates with JWT token, subscribes to 'staffing' channel, and displays the green 'Live' indicator. All existing flows (login, dashboard rendering, staffing grid) continue to work.
passed_tests: Backend WS: Anonymous client connects to wss://.../api/ws and receives {type:'connected', authenticated:false}
Backend WS: Authenticated client (admin token) connects and receives {type:'connected', authenticated:true, user_name:'Admin User'}
Backend WS: subscribe action -> server returns {type:'subscribed', channels:[...]}
Backend WS: ping action -> server returns {type:'pong'}
Backend WS: get_status returns active connection count
Backend Broadcast: POST /api/overtime (200) triggers overtime_update broadcast to subscribed clients within 10s
Frontend: Admin login -> /dashboard URL, page renders
Frontend: WebSocket connects (console: 'WebSocket connected', 'authenticated: true', 'Subscribed to channels: [staffing]')
Frontend: Green 'Live' indicator visible on Dashboard header (Wifi icon + 'Live' text)
Frontend: Existing flows intact - stations grid, minimum staffing, totals, calendar all render correctly
Frontend: REST mutation (POST /api/overtime via authenticated fetch) succeeds (status 200) without breaking WS connection
critical_code_review_comments: websocket_manager.py is clean and well-structured (channel-based pub/sub, per-connection subscription tracking, disconnect cleanup).
WebSocket auth via query token is acceptable (JWT validated server-side). Note: tokens appear in URL/logs - acceptable trade-off since browser WS API does not support custom headers.
Frontend WebSocketContext correctly handles reconnection (3s backoff) and re-subscribes to previously subscribed channels on reconnect.

Dashboard subscribes only to 'staffing' channel via useStaffingUpdates - overtime/personnel updates would NOT trigger Dashboard refresh. This is by design (OvertimePage uses useOvertimeUpdates separately) but worth documenting.
Heartbeat ping every 30s is implemented in frontend - good for keeping connection alive through proxies.

Minor: WebSocketContext.disconnect() returned from useEffect cleanup will trigger on every re-render of provider due to connect/disconnect dependency. In practice this is stable because connect/disconnect are useCallback-memoized, but worth a sanity check during future refactors.
Test credentials file /app/memory/test_credentials.md exists and is accurate (admin: 100001/admin123 worked).
seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_ws_broadcast overtime record (date=today) via /api/overtime POST as part of broadcast verification. Safe to leave; can be cleaned with /api/seed if needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: WebSocket feature is fully working: backend /api/ws endpoint (anon + JWT), channel-based subscribe/unsubscribe, broadcasts on staffing/overtime/apparatus mutations, frontend Live indicator on Dashboard, auto-reconnect with backoff and re-subscribe. Test file: /app/backend/tests/test_websocket.py (4 tests, all passing). When testing UI for real-time updates from a second user, note: Dashboard subscribes only to 'staffing' channel, so overtime mutations won't toast on Dashboard - open OvertimePage to see overtime toasts. Run pytest with REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL env set: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://medina-fire-staffing.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest backend/tests/test_websocket.py -v`.
rca of the issue: N/A - feature working as designed, no issues found.
